experiment.name: Atypical dogs, BET cohort
experiment.description: Two unsupervised anomaly scores over 22 admission variables identify atypical dogs in the BET cohort; every outlier needs a raw-sheet check before interpretation.
experiment.summary: Two unsupervised anomaly scores (isolation forest and robust Mahalanobis distance) were computed for 148 dogs over 22 admission variables; 8 dogs are labelled outlier (combined rank score at or above 0.944). The scores agree with Spearman rho 0.82 (95% interval 0.74 to 0.87) and share 5 of the top 10. Pathogen-minority dogs: BET023 rank 106 (typical), BET072 rank 61 (typical), BET100 rank 17 (typical), BET147 rank 117 (typical). 15 of 15 listed dogs have been checked against the raw sheet (14 match, 0 discrepancy, 1 unit suspect).

sections.heading: Question
paragraphs: Which of the 148 dogs in the DS05 cohort (all Babesia PCR positive; 144 B. rossi only, three B. rossi + E. canis, one B. vogeli only) have an atypical admission profile across 22 routine clinical and laboratory variables, as judged by two unrelated methods (an isolation forest and a robust Mahalanobis distance), do the two methods agree, and do the three B. rossi + E. canis dogs and the one B. vogeli dog stand out? An atypical profile means unusual relative to this cohort. It does not mean abnormal, and there is no outcome in this dataset.

sections.heading: What was done
paragraphs: 150 dogs were available; 2 (BET065, BET066) were not scored because more than 30 percent of the 22 input variables were missing, leaving 148. The inputs are the measured numeric and ordinal admission values; calculated indices (mcv, mch, mchc, wcc, arc, globulin) were left out so that one measurement is not counted twice (they enter sensitivity S3). 15 skewed non-negative variables were log-transformed (age, duration of illness, rectal temperature, haemoglobin, red cell count, haematocrit, red cell distribution width, segmented neutrophils, band neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, platelet count, nucleated red cells, reticulocytes). Nothing was clipped, because extreme values are the object of study. 41 of 3256 cells (1.3 percent) were imputed once by iterative regression, then all variables were standardised.

The isolation forest (1000 trees) was fitted with 10 different seeds and the scores averaged. The robust Mahalanobis distance used the minimum covariance determinant on 22 variables (none had to be dropped). Each score was converted to a rank between 0 (most typical) and 1 (most atypical) and the two were averaged into a combined score. The 8 dogs at or above the 0.95 quantile of the combined score (combined at least 0.944) are labelled outlier; the label depends on ranks, not on a chi-square cut, because skewed data push many dogs (37) over the chi-square 97.5 percent cut of 36.8.

sections.heading: Raw-sheet check
paragraphs: 15 of the 15 listed dogs (top 10, the top 3 of each method and the four pathogen-minority dogs) were checked against the 'Entire population' sheet of the original workbook (and the CORRESPONDENCE sheet for habitus): 14 match the raw sheet, 0 show a discrepancy, 1 look like unit or entry problems in the raw cell, 0 were not checked.

BET026 (rank 1, raw row 28): matches raw. Row 28: seg neutrophils 31.56, band neutrophils 5.46, monocytes 17.6, total protein 94.2 and RCC 5.23 equal the tidy values; the white cell count of 60.69 is the sum of the differential and the MCV agrees with haematocrit and RCC.

BET058 (rank 2, raw row 60): matches raw. Row 60: temperature 33.8, nucleated red cells 113 per 100 WBC, respiratory rate 20, lymphocytes 0.37 and albumin 16.3 equal the tidy values; units follow row 2 and the red cell indices are internally consistent.

BET092 (rank 3, raw row 93): matches raw. Row 93: haematocrit 0.63 L/L, haemoglobin 193 g/L, RCC 9.03 and pulse 160 equal the tidy values; haematocrit, haemoglobin, RCC and the sheet's own MCV and MCHC agree with each other, so this is a recorded high red cell mass, not a unit slip.

BET137 (rank 3, raw row 138): matches raw. Row 138: band neutrophils 12.88, lymphocytes 7.58, reticulocytes 42.9 percent, RDW 28.8, monocytes 0.76 and total protein 34 equal the tidy values; red cell indices are consistent.

BET102 (rank 5, raw row 103): matches raw. Row 103: temperature 33.3, band neutrophils 2.8, age 108 months, segmented neutrophils 21.54, lymphocytes 0.84 and reticulocytes 3.7 equal the tidy values; the low temperature is written as a number in degrees Celsius.

BET020 (rank 6, raw row 22): matches raw. Row 22: band neutrophils 10.46, lymphocytes 7.32, monocytes 8.89, segmented neutrophils 25.63 and total protein 65.7 equal the tidy values; red cell indices are consistent.
BET080 (rank 6, raw row 81): matches raw. Row 81: temperature 34.1, band neutrophils 7.09, albumin 10.3 and RDW 20.7 equal the tidy values; red cell indices are consistent.

BET104 (rank 8, raw row 105): matches raw. Row 105: haemoglobin 18 g/L, haematocrit 0.06 L/L, pulse 200 and reticulocytes 8.2 percent equal the tidy values; haemoglobin and haematocrit agree (MCHC 27.4) so the very severe anaemia is internally consistent.
BET038 (rank 9, raw row 40): matches raw. Row 40: eosinophils 0.66, reticulocytes 0.3 percent, platelets 187, haemoglobin 120 and haematocrit 0.42 equal the tidy values; indices are consistent.
BET050 (rank 10, raw row 52): matches raw. Row 52: respiratory rate 12, RCC 5.68, segmented neutrophils 23.85 and haemoglobin 108 equal the tidy values; indices are consistent.

BET100 (rank 17, raw row 101): matches raw. Row 101 (ID cell reads 'BET100 (B. vogeli)'): segmented neutrophils 0.44, eosinophils 0.01, age 3 months, haematocrit 0.42 and habitus 1+ (CORRESPONDENCE sheet) equal the tidy values; the temperature cell reads LOW (stored as missing) which is not one of the listed drivers.

BET048 (rank 46, raw row 50): unit suspect. Row 50: every listed cell equals the tidy value, but the RCC of 7.89 is identical to the white cell count (7.89) in the same row and is inconsistent with the sheet's own MCV of 75.5 fL, which with haematocrit 0.28 implies an RCC of about 3.7; the RCC cell looks like an entry slip (copied white cell count), so the red cell count is treated as suspect.
BET072 (rank 61, raw row 74): matches raw. Row 74 (ID cell reads 'BET072 (B. rossi + E. canis)'): pulse 72, lymphocytes 0.26 and habitus 1+ (CORRESPONDENCE sheet) equal the tidy values.

BET023 (rank 106, raw row 25): matches raw. Row 25 (ID cell reads 'BET023 (B. rossi + E. canis)'): illness duration 14 days, total protein 74.2, band neutrophils 0.91 and age 8 months equal the tidy values.

BET147 (rank 117, raw row 148): matches raw. Row 148 (ID cell reads 'BET147 (B. rossi + E. canis)'): habitus 1+ (CORRESPONDENCE sheet), illness duration 1 day, reticulocytes 1.1 percent and band neutrophils 1.42 equal the tidy values.

sections.heading: Most atypical dogs
paragraphs: The 8 outlier dogs and the rest of the top 10 by combined score are listed below (rank 1 = most atypical). The cut for the label is a combined score of 0.944.

Rank 1, BET026 (combined 0.997, outlier, top 10 of both methods), main contributors to the distance: monocytes 17.6 x10^9/L (cohort median 0.725, robust z +7.7, above reference); total serum protein 94.2 g/L (cohort median 57.7, robust z +4.0, above reference); red cell count 5.23 x10^12/L (cohort median 2.31, robust z +1.5, below reference).

Rank 2, BET058 (combined 0.980, outlier, top 10 of both methods), main contributors to the distance: rectal temperature 33.8 degrees C (cohort median 40, robust z -9.0); lymphocytes 0.37 x10^9/L (cohort median 1.5, robust z -1.7, below reference); albumin 16.3 g/L (cohort median 23.7, robust z -1.4, below reference).

Rank 3, BET092 (combined 0.976, outlier, top 10 of both methods), main contributors to the distance: haematocrit 0.63 L/L (cohort median 0.18, robust z +4.2, above reference); haemoglobin 193 g/L (cohort median 53, robust z +2.4, above reference); pulse rate 160 per minute (cohort median 132, robust z +1.2).

Rank 3, BET137 (combined 0.976, outlier, top 10 of both methods), main contributors to the distance: band neutrophils 12.9 x10^9/L (cohort median 0.3, robust z +8.2, above reference); monocytes 0.76 x10^9/L (cohort median 0.725, robust z +0.1); total serum protein 34 g/L (cohort median 57.7, robust z -2.6, below reference).

Rank 5, BET102 (combined 0.952, outlier), main contributors to the distance: rectal temperature 33.3 degrees C (cohort median 40, robust z -9.8); lymphocytes 0.84 x10^9/L (cohort median 1.5, robust z -0.8, below reference); reticulocytes 3.7 % (cohort median 3.85, robust z -0.0).

Rank 6, BET020 (combined 0.949, outlier), main contributors to the distance: monocytes 8.89 x10^9/L (cohort median 0.725, robust z +5.7, above reference); total serum protein 65.7 g/L (cohort median 57.7, robust z +0.9); band neutrophils 10.5 x10^9/L (cohort median 0.3, robust z +7.5, above reference).

Rank 6, BET080 (combined 0.949, outlier), main contributors to the distance: rectal temperature 34.1 degrees C (cohort median 40, robust z -8.5); band neutrophils 7.09 x10^9/L (cohort median 0.3, robust z +6.3, above reference); red cell distribution width 20.7 % (cohort median 16.6, robust z +1.1).

Rank 8, BET104 (combined 0.946, outlier), main contributors to the distance: haemoglobin 18 g/L (cohort median 53, robust z -2.0, below reference); haematocrit 0.06 L/L (cohort median 0.18, robust z -1.4, below reference); reticulocytes 8.2 % (cohort median 3.85, robust z +0.6).

Rank 9, BET038 (combined 0.942, typical, top 10 of both methods), main contributors to the distance: eosinophils 0.66 x10^9/L (cohort median 0, robust z +4.6); haemoglobin 120 g/L (cohort median 53, robust z +1.5); haematocrit 0.42 L/L (cohort median 0.18, robust z +2.4).

Rank 10, BET050 (combined 0.935, typical), main contributors to the distance: red cell count 5.68 x10^12/L (cohort median 2.31, robust z +1.7); haemoglobin 108 g/L (cohort median 53, robust z +1.3, below reference); respiratory rate 12 per minute (cohort median 36, robust z -2.0).

Also listed as one of the top 3 of a single method: rank 46, BET048 (combined 0.684, isolation-forest rank 94, Mahalanobis rank 1, typical): data-quality finding, not interpreted biologically (unit suspect). Row 50: every listed cell equals the tidy value, but the RCC of 7.89 is identical to the white cell count (7.89) in the same row and is inconsistent with the sheet's own MCV of 75.5 fL, which with haematocrit 0.28 implies an RCC of about 3.7; the RCC cell looks like an entry slip (copied white cell count), so the red cell count is treated as suspect.
With the suspect raw cells set missing and re-imputed (sensitivity S4) the combined score agrees with the main one at Spearman 0.99; 10 of the top 10 are shared.

sections.heading: The co-infected and B. vogeli dogs
paragraphs: Three dogs, one dog: descriptive only. No test and no group statistic is given; each dog is a single case.

BET023 (B. rossi + E. canis): rank 106 of 148 by combined score 0.303 (isolation forest rank score 0.395, rank 90; Mahalanobis rank score 0.211, rank 117); label typical; raw-sheet check matches raw. Main contributors: duration of illness 14 days (cohort median 3, robust z +3.1); total serum protein 74.2 g/L (cohort median 57.7, robust z +1.8, above reference); age 8 months (cohort median 12, robust z -0.4). The dog's overall profile is not unusual for this cohort.

BET072 (B. rossi + E. canis): rank 61 of 148 by combined score 0.578 (isolation forest rank score 0.687, rank 47; Mahalanobis rank score 0.469, rank 79); label typical; raw-sheet check matches raw. Main contributors: habitus (mental status) score 1 (cohort median 2, robust z -0.7); pulse rate 72 per minute (cohort median 132, robust z -2.5); lymphocytes 0.26 x10^9/L (cohort median 1.5, robust z -1.9, below reference). The dog's overall profile is not unusual for this cohort.

BET100 (B. vogeli only): rank 17 of 148 by combined score 0.888 (isolation forest rank score 0.925, rank 12; Mahalanobis rank score 0.850, rank 23); label typical; raw-sheet check matches raw. Main contributors: habitus (mental status) score 1 (cohort median 2, robust z -0.7); segmented neutrophils 0.44 x10^9/L (cohort median 5.23, robust z -2.7, below reference); haematocrit 0.42 L/L (cohort median 0.18, robust z +2.4).

BET147 (B. rossi + E. canis): rank 117 of 148 by combined score 0.248 (isolation forest rank score 0.374, rank 93; Mahalanobis rank score 0.122, rank 130); label typical; raw-sheet check matches raw. Main contributors: habitus (mental status) score 1 (cohort median 2, robust z -0.7); duration of illness 1 day (cohort median 3, robust z -1.6); band neutrophils 1.42 x10^9/L (cohort median 0.3, robust z +2.2, above reference). The dog's overall profile is not unusual for this cohort.

0 of the four are among the top 10. A finding that none of them is among the top outliers is a valid negative result: co-infection or a different Babesia species need not move routine admission variables.

sections.heading: Agreement between the two methods
paragraphs: Spearman correlation between the two rank scores is 0.82 (95 percent bootstrap interval 0.74 to 0.87, permutation p < 0.001). 5 of the top 10 are shared (Jaccard 0.33); 4 of the top 8 (5 percent) and 17 of the top 20.
Only in the isolation-forest top 10: BET020, BET042, BET050, BET104, BET126. Only in the Mahalanobis top 10: BET018, BET048, BET057, BET080, BET102.

The two methods broadly agree, though they reward different kinds of unusualness: in the injection test the Mahalanobis distance reacted strongly to one extreme value in a correlated set, while the forest's random feature choice dilutes a single extreme among 22 variables and rewards dogs that are unusual on several variables at once.
Sensitivity S1_complete_case (n = 113): Spearman with the main combined score 0.96, 10 of the top 10 shared; pathogen-minority bands: BET023 rest, BET072 rest, BET100 not in sample, BET147 rest.
Sensitivity S2_no_log_transform (n = 148): Spearman with the main combined score 0.91, 7 of the top 10 shared; pathogen-minority bands: BET023 rest, BET072 rest, BET100 rest, BET147 rest.

Sensitivity S3_with_derived_variables (n = 148): Spearman with the main combined score 0.90, 6 of the top 10 shared; pathogen-minority bands: BET023 rest, BET072 top20pct, BET100 top20pct, BET147 rest.

Sensitivity S4_suspect_cells_set_missing (n = 148): Spearman with the main combined score 0.99, 10 of the top 10 shared; pathogen-minority bands: BET023 rest, BET072 rest, BET100 top20pct, BET147 rest.

sections.heading: Limits
paragraphs: Unsupervised outlier scores say a dog is unusual relative to this cohort. They do not say a dog is clinically abnormal or will do badly; no outcome exists in this dataset and the scores are not prognostic. Outliers are as likely to be data-entry, unit or transcription problems as biology, which is why each listed dog was compared with the raw sheet.
The isolation forest is stable between seeds: the minimum pairwise Spearman across 10 seeds is 0.989 (reported score is the mean of the fits).
A dog with a single wildly wrong value may rank high on one method only (the Mahalanobis distance picks it up far more readily than the isolation forest), which is why both lists are shown.

41 cells were imputed; a driver whose value was imputed is flagged. Skewed haematology means the chi-square cut over-flags (37 dogs), so the label uses ranks. One hospital cohort of 148 dogs and 22 correlated variables; the isolation forest is not tuned. The raw-sheet check covers only the listed dogs, not the remaining 133, and a veterinarian should review any discrepancy or unit-suspect dog before the page is shared.

payload.excluded_other: All C, D and T variables, basophils, other_cells and month; mcv, mch, mchc, wcc, arc and globulin are arithmetic functions of other columns and are used only in sensitivity S3.

no haematology or biochemistry; 15 of 22 input variables missing

imputation.method: IterativeImputer(BayesianRidge, max_iter=20, initial_strategy=median) once on the standardised matrix; matrix re-standardised afterwards

dataset.licence: CC BY 4.0, taken from the known Figshare record metadata supplied with the task. Not re-read from the live record.

notes: Ordinal variables (lymph_node_score, habitus_score) treated as numeric.

Transformed variables (log1p): age_months, illness_days, temperature_c, haemoglobin, rcc, haematocrit, rdw, seg_neutrophils, band_neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, platelets, nrbc_per_100_wbc, reticulocyte_pct. No clipping or winsorising.
Imputed driver values are back-transformed estimates and flagged imputed = true.
cohort_median is the median of observed original-unit values among scored dogs.
reason_listed joins every reason with '+'; label threshold is the 0.95 quantile of the combined score.
